verdict: Truist's headline profit fell to $799M because it booked a $1.4B loss selling securities to reposition its balance sheet — underneath, adjusted EPS rose 12% to $1.16 and net interest income held steady at $3.7B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: GAAP revenue $3.7B, hit by the $1.4B securities loss; adjusted revenue was stable at about $5.3B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: adjusted EPS $1.16, up 12% YoY, excluding the securities loss and reserve release

kpis.label: Net interest income
kpis.note: +1% YoY; margin 3.00% on a taxable-equivalent basis

kpis.label: Credit costs
kpis.note: a $581M reserve release from the RAC loan sale more than covered $629M of charge-offs

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, roughly flat as balances held up.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and other income — crushed this quarter by $1,447M of losses on securities sold to reposition the portfolio, which swamped record wealth-management income of $407M.

opex.name: Personnel expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Truist's workforce — its biggest cost by far.

opex.name: Professional & other services
opex.note: Outside professional services ($365M) plus other noninterest expense ($376M) — legal, consulting and miscellaneous running costs.

opex.name: Occupancy & equipment
opex.note: Branch and office occupancy ($180M) plus software and equipment ($331M).

oneTimers: $1,447M pre-tax loss on the sale of available-for-sale securities, booked as part of a balance-sheet repositioning after the Regional Acceptance Corporation (RAC) loan sale — the main reason GAAP EPS was $0.56 vs adjusted EPS of $1.16.

A $581M pre-tax benefit inside credit costs from releasing loan-loss reserves after the RAC loan sale, plus $106M of other RAC sale impacts and $40M of RAC sale costs in expenses. Excluding all flagged items, net income available to common shareholders was $1.42B instead of $684M.
footerNote: For a bank, the provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue. This quarter it was a $253M benefit (money added back, not spent) because selling the RAC loan book released $581M of reserves — so the amount after credit costs ($4,000M) is larger than revenue itself. Net income of $799M is before $115M of preferred dividends, leaving $684M for common shareholders.

takeaways.title: The underlying quarter was solid
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $1.16, up 12% from a year ago, and adjusted revenue was stable at about $5.3B — the GAAP drop is the securities repositioning, not the business shrinking.

takeaways.title: A deliberate, one-off hit
takeaways.text: Truist sold securities at a $1,447M loss to reposition its balance sheet after selling the RAC auto-loan book, and agreed on October 14 to sell $7.7B of LightStream unsecured loans as well.

takeaways.title: Credit cover got thinner — by design
takeaways.text: The allowance for loan and lease losses fell to 1.25% of loans from 1.54% a year ago, mostly because the riskier RAC loans left the book. Charge-offs were 0.77% annualized, including RAC effects.
